overall.summary: The plain hypothesis for the a5 part (always turns the prediction to 'no') is contradicted by the model, and the veto's and gate's technical hypotheses carry wrong numbers (veto switching on at two instead of three first values; 52 instead of 40 clipped rows). Everything else, including all 65 claims, reproduces.

findings.statement: with one or fewer indicators the pre-activation is at most -0.2 (exactly 0 output), with two it is at least +5.6 ... on all 345 training rows 274 > 0 exactly when two or more of a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 take their first value (112 rows)
findings.check: node 274 pre-activation by count of first values (weights and scaler from the replayed model); enumerate all 432 configurations; subgroup counts on train
findings.evidence: Pre-activation by count: 0: -19.2; 1: -12.0..-9.5; 2: -3.4..-0.2; 3: +5.6..+8.8. Node 274 fires on 0/152 two-count configurations and on all 100/32/4 with 3/4/5. On train it fires on 112 rows = rows with three or more first values (112); rows with two or more number 236. The veto switches on at three, not two (the part's own name and its evidence record say three).

findings.evidence: 0 for at most two (true); for exactly three the exit is -58.2 to -93.3, so '<= -70' is not a bound. The sign conclusion (score negative for three or more) still holds.

findings.evidence: The subgroup a5 = 1 and a3 = 2 has 40 training rows, and the gate is off on exactly those 40 (active 0 of 40 vs 100% elsewhere; 305 active rows = C47). The 'exactly when' part holds (54/54 configurations), the count 52 does not; the part's evidence record correctly says 40.

findings.statement: This part decides the outcome whenever a5 = 2 or 4: it always turns the prediction to 'no'.
findings.check: subgroup a5 in {2,4} with predicted risk >= 0.5; ablation of the part; probe a5 x a3 at the typical case
findings.evidence: 64 of the 173 training cases with a5 = 2 or 4 are predicted 'yes' (mean risk 97.1%). Switching the part off flips 1 of 345 predictions (accuracy 0.887 -> 0.890, AUC unchanged); its contribution is a fixed -0.72 on the score. Typical case with a3 = 2 and a5 = 2: risk 100% (score +9.6), part contributes -0.72. The cited claims only say a5 = 2 or 4 lowers the probability; the technical hypothesis itself calls it a small penalty.
